claim_verdicts.evidence: Đơn Hàng part holds: DonHangDbContext has no Entity<Vnd>/DbSet<Vnd>; executed scratch model with the same mapping: `model has entity Vnd: False`. But 'so it cannot have rows of its own' is contradicted in general for efcore: owned-entities.md:134 'owned types can be stored in a separate table from the owner', keyed by a shadow key equal to the owner's key (:50). No id means nothing in it is its own key, not that it cannot have rows.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: A value object has no id of its own, so nothing in it can serve as its own key. In Đơn Hàng, Vnd holds a single value and is mapped with a value converter into its owner's row: no table or key of its own; its amount is a column of order_items.

claim_verdicts.evidence: "Value converters allow property values to be converted when reading from or writing to the database." (:10); "Conversions are defined using two Func expression trees: one from ModelClrType to ProviderClrType and the other from ProviderClrType to ModelClrType." issues.text: Claim 3 overstates EF Core: 'it cannot have rows of its own' is false in general for efcore 10 - owned-entities.md:134 'owned types can be stored in a separate table from the owner', with a shadow key copied from the owner (:50). True: nothing in a value object is its own key, and Đơn Hàng chose a converter. Owned types are out of scope (depth_notes), so narrow the wording; do not mention them. Same finding as the previous technical round; the sentence came back with the junior fix.
issues.quote: With nothing to use as a key it cannot have rows of its own, so Đơn Hàng maps `Vnd` with a value converter into its owner's row
issues.fix: Replace with: "Nothing in it can serve as a key, so Đơn Hàng gives `Vnd` no rows of its own: a value converter maps it into its owner's row". Set claim 3 text in .meta.json to this review's suggested_text for claim 3.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: a gloss of three EF Core APIs, not in the claims ledger. It is supportable: entity-types.md:52 'You can manually configure the table name:'; keys.md:21 'You can configure a single property to be the primary key of an entity', :33 multiple properties form a composite key.
issues.quote: For `OrderItem`, `Entity<OrderItem>` declares a mapped class, `ToTable` names its table and `HasKey` sets its primary key.
issues.fix: Add a claim to .meta.json: kind "behavior", version_key "efcore", section 5, text "In OnModelCreating, Entity<T>() configures entity type T, ToTable sets its table name and HasKey configures its primary key (several properties give a composite key)", source_hint "EF Core docs: Entity Types (Table name); Keys". issues.text: Unlisted claim, and too absolute: EF Core can also create the schema with EnsureCreated, and SQL run by hand changes a column; neither is a migration. True of Đơn Hàng, whose schema evolves through DonHang.Infrastructure/Migrations, not of databases in general.
issues.quote: The real column in the database changes only when a migration changes it.
issues.fix: Replace with: "In Đơn Hàng, the real column changes only when a migration changes it."
